cards.front: Recall a key point about Consumer Rights
cards.back: The Consumer Rights Act 2015 is the main law protecting consumers in contracts with businesses

cards.front: Recall a key point about Consumer Rights
cards.back: Goods must be of satisfactory quality, fit for purpose and as described — if not, the consumer has rights to reject, repair or replacement

cards.front: Recall a key point about Consumer Rights
cards.back: For faulty goods, the consumer has 30 days to reject for a full refund; after 30 days, they can request repair or replacement

cards.front: Recall a key point about Consumer Rights
cards.back: If a repair or replacement fails, the consumer is entitled to a refund (which may be reduced for use)

cards.front: Recall a key point about Consumer Rights
cards.back: Services must be performed with reasonable care and skill, within a reasonable time and at a reasonable price

cards.front: Recall a key point about Consumer Rights
cards.back: Digital content (downloads, apps, games) must also be of satisfactory quality, fit for purpose and as described under the 2015 Act

cards.front: Recall a key point about Consumer Rights
cards.back: Unfair terms in consumer contracts are not binding on the consumer — terms that create a significant imbalance favouring the trader are unfair

cards.front: Recall a key point about Consumer Rights
cards.back: The trader cannot exclude liability for death or personal injury caused by negligence — other exclusions must be reasonable

cards.front: Recall a key point about Consumer Rights
cards.back: Trading Standards enforces consumer protection law — it can prosecute rogue traders and advise consumers

cards.front: Recall a key point about Consumer Rights
cards.back: Citizens Advice provides free consumer advice and can help resolve disputes with traders

cards.front: Recall a key point about Consumer Rights
cards.back: Misrepresentation is a false statement of fact that induces a person into a contract — remedies include rescission and damages

cards.front: Recall a key point about Consumer Rights
cards.back: The Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) investigates anti-competitive practices and enforces consumer law at a national level

cards.front: What should you know about gcse law exam tips — consumer rights?
cards.back: 1. For Consumer Rights questions, identify the relevant area of law and state the legal principles clearly 2. Apply legal rules to the facts of the scenario — don't just state the law 3. When evaluating, consider both the effectiveness and fairness of legal rules 4. Reference relevant cases and statutes when discussing Consumer Rights 5. Consider reform proposals and alternative approaches where relevant
